extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and artist-researchers applying to SSHRC Insight Grants or Insight Development Grants for research-creation projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing research-creation applications to SSHRC Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants, covering eligibility, required proposal content, support materials, assessment criteria, and final submission checks. Targeted to researcher/artist teams proposing integrated creative and scholarly projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: SSHRC mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a proposal, determine whether the proposed research falls within SSHRC’s mandate. The objectives and outcomes of the proposed project should be related to the social sciences and the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If working with new technologies, or within the scientific or architectural fields, take care to ensure the research falls within SSHRC's mandate and not that of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC). First-time applicants may contact their institution's research office or the relevant SSHRC program officer to clarify eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/scope of research-creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Research-creation is an approach that combines creative and academic research practices and represents sustained, reflective research set directly and actively within the creation process itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should contain both a developed scholarly apparatus and an integral connection to contemporary literary/artistic practices. Research exclusively about the creation process or about literary/artistic productions, or creative work involving minimal scholarly investigation, will not be considered to fall within the scope of research-creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core proposal requirements (research questions, theory, method/creation process)
rubrics_metrics.description: A research-creation proposal must: address clear research questions; offer theoretical contextualization within the relevant fields of inquiry; and present a well-considered methodological approach and creation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should clearly demonstrate how the research informs the creation process, as well as how the creation process is integrated into and relevant to the project. The theory and methodology must be aligned with the proposal’s objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly and creative excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the research and any resulting creative work must meet peer standards of excellence and be suitable for publication, public performance and/or viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure proposed research outputs and creative works adhere to discipline-specific peer standards and are presented at a level appropriate for public dissemination or exhibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate feasibility and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must show that their proposed project is well thought out and can be carried out as planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a coherent plan linking objectives, theory, methodology and creative activities so reviewers can judge viability and realistic timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant background and avoid assuming reviewer familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide relevant background information and should not presume adjudication committee members are familiar with the work, or with the specific terminology and particularities of the field of specialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain key terms, context and prior work succinctly so a multidisciplinary committee can assess the proposal without specialized prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and clarity of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be concise and to the point, and avoid lengthy or vague statements about the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, direct language; avoid unnecessary jargon and long digressions. Emphasize the central research questions, methods and expected contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support material: web-based samples and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicants identify their proposal as research-creation, they must include a website link to samples of work that best illustrate the qualifications of the team and/or the nature of the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the link and any related information in the appropriate section of the application form. Ensure the website is of the best possible quality and that all links will be operational for at least six months after the application deadline. SSHRC will make reasonable efforts to view/listen to support material but cannot guarantee access; SSHRC assumes no responsibility if links are broken or servers unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment framework: Challenge, Feasibility, Capability
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must meet the Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants evaluation criteria; SSHRC’s Challenge, Feasibility and Capability evaluation criteria form the basis for the merit review committee’s decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the proposal to address these three areas: the intellectual challenge and contribution (Challenge), the soundness and practicability of methods and plan (Feasibility), and the expertise, track record and environment of the investigators (Capability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate multidisciplinary merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight Grant and Insight Development Grant applications involving research-creation are typically adjudicated by a multidisciplinary merit review committee structured to ensure representation of expert knowledge from a broad range of fields and regional, linguistic, cultural and gender balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare materials that communicate significance and methods to reviewers across disciplines and cultural/linguistic backgrounds; justify specialized approaches for non-specialist readers where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Indigenous research considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should discuss considerations, ethics standards and requirements related to research involving humans and, more specifically, research involving Research Involving the First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples of Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult institutional ethics offices and relevant SSHRC/agency guidelines on Indigenous research protocols and human-subjects ethics; include necessary approvals or plans to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget realism and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must ensure that their budget is realistic and well-justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If artists are paid as consultants or participants, fees should comply with the principal investigator’s institutional requirements. Applicants are advised to consult artist representation agencies (e.g., CARFAC, Union des artistes, Canadian Actors’ Equity Association) for guidance on appropriate fees and norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and institutional submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must ensure that their application is complete; incomplete applications are automatically ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the completed application to the institution’s research office by the office’s internal deadline. Double-check all required sections, forms and attachments before institutional submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation quality: spelling and copy-editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must make sure their text is free of spelling errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully proofread and copy-edit the proposal to avoid avoidable errors that can undermine reviewer confidence in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles of professional artists and contractual/fee considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional artists may participate as research collaborators, consultants and/or professional service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When artists are paid, ensure fees follow institutional requirements and reflect industry standards; consult artist representation agencies for detailed information about artists’ fees and contractual norms.
